title: Robust Uplift Modeling with Large-Scale Contexts for Real-time Marketing

problem.claim: Online marketing platforms need to improve user engagement and revenue by assigning treatments to users, potentially in the presence of item-specific contexts.

gap.claim: Existing uplift modeling commonly relies only on user features, while large-scale contexts can bias response predictions and cause treatment-control distribution shifts when directly concatenated with user features.

contributions.claim: A model-agnostic UMLC framework is proposed for robust uplift modeling with large-scale contexts in real-time marketing.
The framework combines response-guided context grouping with feature interaction modeling, including user-context and treatment-feature interaction components.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe UMLC as a novel model-agnostic framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on a synthetic dataset and a real-world product dataset to verify UMLC's effectiveness and compatibility.

narrative_sequence.summary: Improving engagement and revenue is important for online marketing platforms, motivating treatment-based uplift modeling.
Existing approaches are limited by user-only features and by the difficulties of incorporating rich, large-scale contexts.
UMLC addresses these limitations through context grouping and feature interaction modules for robust uplift prediction.
The authors evaluate UMLC on synthetic and real-world product datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results or baselines.
The abstract does not describe the datasets, treatment definitions, or evaluation metrics.
